THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,

 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 28.03.2013 in MVC.No.11/2011 passed by the Fast Track Judge and Addl. MACT at KGF., for seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. In the present case, the Tribunal has fastened the liability on respondent No.1-owner.
3. In the present case, the driver of the Autorickshaw (transport) was holding driving licence to drive LMV (non-transport).
The issue involved in the present case is no more res integra.
Therefore, the driver who was holding the driving licence to drive LMV (non- transport) is also competent to drive LMV (transport).
Therefore, the issue involved is squarely covered by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of MUKUND DEWANGAN VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1.

In the present case, from the wound certificate coupled with doctor's evidence, it is proved that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
i. comminuted fracture of left patella ii. Abrasion over left knee 6.
In the present case, the claimant was aged 46 years as on the date of the accident and met with an accident.
The claimant is a tailor by profession and was earning income of Rs.15,000/- pm.
The doctor-P.W.2 has stated that the claimant has suffered 36% of permanent physical disability towards left lower limb and 12% towards whole body.
The fracture is caused to the left patella.
Certainly, this type of fracture to the patella bone affects the day to day activity and finding difficulty in doing tailoring work.
It cannot be expected documentary proof regarding avocation of tailor to be carried out by the claimant.

Therefore, just because, there is no document regarding tailoring work,
it cannot be said that the claimant was not doing tailoring work.
Therefore, certainly, the loss of earning capacity is affected due to the said disability.
Hence, as per the evidence of doctor, it is held that the claimant had suffered functional disability at 12%.
Just because, the claimant is able to climb stairs and was able to stand for 40 minutes in witness box, it does not mean what the claimant had not suffered disability.
The observation made by the Tribunal in this regard is not correct.

Therefore, by following the principle of law laid down in the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another 2, functional disability at 12% is taken into consideration.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another 2, functional disability at 12%
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As the accident occurred in the year 2011, the notional income of the claimant is to be taken at Rs.6,500/- per month as per the Notional Income Chart recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
As the claimant is aged 46 years as on the date of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is 13.

Hence, the compensation under the head loss of (2011) 1 SCC 343 future income due to disability is reassessed and quantified as follows:
Rs.6,500/- x 12% x 13 x 12=Rs.1,21,680/-
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.1,21,680/- is awarded under the head loss of future income due to disability.

Hence, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,48,180/- (Rs.2,81,180/- - Rs.1,33,000/-).

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,48,180/-along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

iii. The appellant/claimant is not entitled for interest for the delay period of 884 days in filing the appeal.
vi. No order as to costs.
